fields.notes: Wishbone B4 does NOT specify DFT / scan / BIST / MBIST / boundary scan. The protocol only specifies functional bus signaling. It is explicitly written to be 'Independent of FPGA and ASIC test methodologies' (1.1 WISHBONE Features). Concrete Wishbone-compliant IP cores add standard scan insertion + DFT compression + boundary-scan during SoC integration; debug visibility is typically provided via JTAG (IEEE 1149.1), CoreSight, SignalTap (FPGA), or similar — all outside the scope of this bus protocol spec.
fields.spec_provided_observability_for_test_pur: The reset signal [RST_O] is also intended for test simulation purposes (Section 3.1.1): the reset cycle can be used to initialize all self-starting state machines and counters in the design. This is the closest the spec gets to a 'test' mechanism — it is purely functional, not DFT.
fields.fault_detection_features_optional: The spec defines [ERR_I]/[ERR_O] for abnormal cycle termination (e.g. parity faults detected by SLAVE circuitry) and [RTY_I]/[RTY_O] for retry termination, but the actual fault-detection mechanism (parity, ECC, watchdog) is IP-supplier-defined and entirely outside the bus protocol layer.

evidence.quote: Independent of FPGA and ASIC test methodologies.
The reset signal [RST_O] is driven by the SYSCON module. It is also used for test simulation purposes by initializing all self-starting state machines and counters which may be used in the design.
